name: Conversions API (server to server events)
plain: Advertisers send purchase and lead events straight from their servers with hashed identifiers.
meaning: Moves tracking off the browser where blockers and cookie limits apply. LinkedIn matches events to members using hashed email, click ID, IP hash and other IDs.

access.persistence: Mapping of externalIds kept 1 year; events must be within 90 days
steps: Create a rule with conversionMethod CONVERSIONS_API (POST /rest/conversions)
Server sends events with user.userIds and userInfo
LinkedIn deduplicates on eventId and matches to members
Rate limits 600 per minute and 500,000 per day; scopes rw_conversions and r_ads

fields.name: idType
fields.range: SHA256_EMAIL, LINKEDIN_FIRST_PARTY_ADS_TRACKING_UUID, ACXIOM_ID, PLAINTEXT_IP_ADDRESS, SHA256_IP_ADDRESS, GOOGLE_AID

fields.name: userInfo
fields.range: firstName, lastName, hashed names (from 202609), companyName, title, countryCode

limits.headline: Can send your purchases and sign ups to LinkedIn from a company's servers
limits.user_action: Nothing on your side. It happens after you buy or sign up on an advertiser's site
can: Send a purchase or lead event straight from the advertiser's servers to LinkedIn
Include a scrambled version of your email or other details to match you to a member
Count conversions even if your browser blocks tracking scripts
Report events that happened days after the ad click
cannot: Be seen or blocked by your browser, since it never touches your device
Match you without the advertiser having your details or click ID
Be switched off by a cookie banner choice alone, unless the advertiser honors it
Send events from sites that have not set it up

story.what_it_is: Advertisers tell LinkedIn about your purchase or sign up from their own servers, not your browser.

marketing.name: Conversions API
marketing.pitch: LinkedIn pitches it as a way for advertisers to send conversion data directly, for more complete measurement as browser tracking weakens.

story.for_you: You never see it. After you fill in a form or buy something, the company's server quietly sends LinkedIn a note with a scrambled version of your email. Your browser cannot block it, because it never passes through your browser.
story.for_makers: Browsers and blockers cut what scripts can see, so advertisers lose sales they used to count. A server to server note fills the gap and lets LinkedIn match the sale to an ad. It also lets a company report offline leads, such as a signed contract after a sales call.

use_cases.example: A software company sends LinkedIn the name of each lead that turns into a paid customer, so the ad team sees which campaign paid off.
A marketing team compares LinkedIn reported sales to its own records, using server events that skip ad blockers.
A B2B firm tells LinkedIn when a sales rep closes a deal weeks after the web form, linking it to the first ad click.
An online shop sends a purchase event from checkout servers so a sale still counts when a shopper uses a blocker.
The company hashes your email on its server before sending, which it says protects privacy, though the hash still identifies you.
A university sends LinkedIn an event when a prospect finishes an application, to find more people like them.

risks: Cannot be blocked in your browser

technical_bounds: Not a browser mechanism: needs the advertiser's server
Old ORACLE_MOAT_ID is not in the current schema

abuse: Hidden matching of customers to LinkedIn profiles

linkedin.how: Server side companion to the Insight Tag, documented on Microsoft Learn.
